candidates: When writing shell command examples in documentation, do not use `python3` as the Python interpreter command — it opens the Windows Store on Windows. Prefer `python` where the environment is controlled, or use the `ase` CLI; add a note if interpreter availability varies by platform.

Whenever documentation prose describes instantiating a calculator profile (e.g., `XxxProfile(command=...)`), always accompany the explanation with a complete, minimal, runnable code block showing the exact call syntax rather than relying on prose description alone.

When documenting how to configure any calculator via a profile, mention `BaseProfile` (with a hyperlink to its API docs) so that users unfamiliar with class inheritance understand which constructor arguments are shared across all calculator profiles.

Break long 'Calculator configuration' documentation sections into clearly labeled subsections — at minimum 'Configuration file', 'Environment variable' (with a concrete export example), and 'Profile instantiation' — to improve navigability for users who want only one of those mechanisms.

In all developer and contributing documentation that describes how to implement a calculator, reference `GenericFileIOCalculator` as the currently recommended base class for IO-based calculators, not the older `FileIOCalculator`. Any planned developer guide on 'Designing a custom calculator' should also make this the primary recommendation.

All code examples that instantiate a profile object (e.g., `OrcaProfile`, `AbinitProfile`, `EspressoProfile`) must use explicit keyword argument names (e.g., `OrcaProfile(command='/path/to/orca')`) rather than positional arguments, both for readability and to ensure examples remain correct if the constructor gains new parameters later.

When a feature or parameter is deprecated or removed (e.g., `parallel_info`), search all calculator documentation pages for remaining references to that feature and update or remove them in the same MR or an immediately following one, rather than leaving stale references scattered across individual calculator pages.
